evidence: DRAFT, not signed: the owner's review and signature are still to come, and the release integrator (#258) replaces this branch's declaration with one combined declaration for 0128-0137 (exactly those files plus the merged runtime-grants.sql, with its new sha256). Migrations 0133_own_facility_pharmacy_and_lab_work.sql (sha256 177f07572d161d1be867b8d9fc92585efd35808a499a9b20b70bc9cc9fa40cdf) and 0134_sealed_qa_hospital_pharmacy_lab_staff.sql (sha256 13a58405e179befac7eb3e1854862b33787e040177a48fa98f55557b2cedb5b7) and their runtime-grants.sql block (file sha256 213bfc253a6c4d21d163bb561090f37be1d8fba14072bcb6f85afddb7ee4f225; the second review round added ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed's grant and the withdrawal trigger function's PUBLIC revoke). WHAT 0133 DOES: identity.facility_work_member_allows (direct care, the row's facility is the session's, <kind>.work-item.read and <kind>.order-route.receive held there, which today only the pharmacist and lab roles hold, the patient active, no deny directive); the work items' read policies gain it for own items (no order route), for reads only; 0124's patient cards gain it; the work chain gains 42 permissive own_work_* policies decided item by item; 0086's context_allows are unchanged, so the imported evidence, the Lab outbox and the route reports gain nothing and a route-backed item's rows never pass; pharmacy.own_prescription_sends (row-level security on, no policy, no grant); ehr.send_prescription_to_own_pharmacy for the EHR runtime (pharmacy-api's own PharmacyWorkItemCreated payload) and ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed (its no_pharmacy test alone, read only, for the prescription list and page); the withdrawal: a trigger on ehr.prescriptions (prescriptions_own_pharmacy_send_withdrawn, its SECURITY DEFINER function the owner's alone) records a sent prescription held, cancelled, entered in error, edited or resumed whichever ehr-api image changes it, and ehr.withdraw_own_pharmacy_send and the pharmacy list's states report it only while the item is not dispensed; the own-work access check answers the audit basis (consent for a member holding its own grant for the action, else own-work, as the list's reader does); two ehr.prescriptions policies for the dispensing validator's owner only. UNDO (by hand only): drop the withdrawal trigger and its function before the sends table, or every later prescription status or version change fails (42P01); 0133's header gives the order. WHAT 0134 DOES: where 0123 installed the sealed QA tenant (Amazon RDS: production and staging) the QA Pharmacist and QA Lab Scientist logins gain a pharmacist and a lab membership at QA Hospital; a login that is not 0123's now, or one the QA Facility Admin already gave that role at QA Hospital (active or not), is left alone with a notice instead of stopping the release; elsewhere nothing. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's images call none of the new functions; through the changed policies today's lab-api and pharmacy-api list the facility's own items for its pharmacy and lab staff and record them as 0124 did (with OWN_WORK_PATIENT_CARD_ENABLED on, a per-patient row with basis consent even for a member without a grant; off, the default, the collection row only) until the new images serve: deploy them with 0133 (whether they should go out before the migration, and whether a rollback of one alone may stand after it, is an open owner question); a single item, a dispensing and every chain command still ask Identity's consent in today's images; the withdrawal is the database's, so today's ehr-api images mark it too; ehr-api answers ownPharmacyStaffed and pharmacyHandoff only where 0133 is applied. LOCKS: 0133 takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.prescriptions and the 20 chain tables (and ACCESS SHARE on six tables its SQL functions read) NOWAIT; first in its transaction (the runner applies each file in its own) it retries every 100 ms for at most 5 s, else 55P03 with nothing of 0133 applied; when its transaction already holds another migration's table locks (the runner's dry run of 0128-0137 in one transaction) it makes one attempt and no sleep; in that dry run the locks of every file last until it ends, and a later file that waits for its own locks (0136's plain LOCK TABLE of auth.permissions, auth.role_permissions and identity.access_requests, up to the runner's 5 s lock_timeout) keeps them held meanwhile, which the combined declaration must state (the dry run belongs in a quiet window). 0134 writes at most two rows in each of two tables, only where the QA tenant is installed. PROVED (local, throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15, synthetic data, after the second review round, at 6ce0d24a, the head that last changed code; ac8bd8a1 and this commit change only ORD-2's text and this evidence): the TUF staging rehearsal passed (3 min 53 s; 0028 -> 0134 upgrade, 599 foreign keys, 0 orphans, restore equal; order_routes, records_processing, own_work_patient_cards, prescription_details and own_facility_work runtime checks pass through the booted services as their exact runtime roles, the own-facility check now also editing a dispensed prescription and probing the chart with reads each role permits, the cards check now asserting that another facility's pharmacist and lab member see none of the hospital's own work); a fresh install of 0001-0127 + 0133 + 0134 as a superuser and as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (plan, dry run rolled back, apply, bootstrap, verify-only, 0 pending); all 102 database suites pass on the superuser build and 100 of 102 on the NOBYPASSRLS build (schema's job_events case and records-processing-draft case 6n, which fail the same way on staging 1f5e2c2a itself); on staging 1f5e2c2a's 128 files applied by its own runner as the NOBYPASSRLS migrator the plan is exactly [0133, 0134], the dry run rolls back with privileges unchanged, the apply takes 207 ms (0133 53 ms), a second run answers 'already applied', the release adds exactly 27 EXECUTE grants and removes none, this branch's runtime-grants.sql changes nothing after it, and the suites answer 100 of 102 as on staging; the refusals answer their own messages (each missing marker, a missing column, a changed or missing relied-on body, a table of another owner, non-owner appliers, a hid_ role that is the owner's member, 0134 without 0133), nothing applied; behind a conflicting lock on each of the 27 tables 0133 stops after about 5 s with 55P03 while writers finish in 11-28 ms, and behind a 2 s reader it retries and applies; with another migration's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE already held in the same transaction it stops in 29 ms and a consent_grants reader waits 14 ms; The second round's new cases fail on the code before them: the after-dispensing withdrawal (suite case 7e, got true), ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed (case 2b, no such function), the superseded reason and ownPharmacyStaffed (ehr-api specs), and the cards check against a deliberately facility-blind 0133 (the previous check passed it). COLLATE "C"), so they hold whatever the database's default collation is; proved by applying 0001-0127, 0133 and 0134 as a superuser with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds (as the database-migration image test does) on a cluster whose default collation is ICU en-US with punctuation ignored, like the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image's en_US.utf8, where the file before this change stopped with '0133: the keys of pharmacy.own_prescription_sends are not this file''s' and now applies, runtime-grants.sql applies, and every database suite (17 + 85) passes.
